extraction.name: Vibravox
extraction.description: Vibravox is a dataset compliant with the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) containing audio recordings using five different body-conduction audio sensors: two in-ear microphones, two bone conduction vibration pickups, and a laryngophone. The dataset also includes audio data from an airborne microphone used as a reference. The Vibravox corpus contains 45 hours per sensor of speech samples and physiological sounds recorded by 188 participants under different acoustic conditions imposed by a high order ambisonics 3D spatializer. Annotations about the recording conditions and linguistic transcriptions are also included in the corpus.
extraction.creator: Julien Hauret, Malo Olivier, Thomas Joubaud, Christophe Langrenne, Sarah Poirée, Véronique Zimpfer, and Eric Bavu
extraction.publisher: Laboratoire de Mécanique des Structures et des Systèmes Couplés, Conservatoire national des arts et métiers, HESAM Université
extraction.citeAs: Vibravox: A Dataset of French Speech Captured with Body-conduction Audio Sensors
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The Vibravox dataset was developed through a rigorous data collection process involving 200 participants, with 188 retained after post-processing to ensure high-quality data. The recording process included four steps: speech-clean (participants read sentences for 15 minutes), speechless-noisy (participants remained silent in a noisy environment for 2 minutes and 24 seconds), speechless-clean (participants remained silent in complete silence for 54 seconds), and speech-noisy (participants spoke in a noisy environment for 54 seconds). The dataset includes recordings from five body-conduction sensors and one airborne microphone as a reference, with all six sensors recording simultaneously. The noise was spatialized using a 3D sound spatializer with 56 loudspeakers, and the noise samples were sourced from Audio Set and in-house recordings of concerts and street events.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Physical data collection, Experiments, Software Collection
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: The raw data collection involved five body-conduction audio sensors (two in-ear microphones, two bone conduction vibration pickups, and a laryngophone) and one airborne microphone as a reference. The sensors included a headset microphone, forehead accelerometer, in-ear soft foam microphone, in-ear rigid earpiece microphone, throat microphone, and temple vibration pickup. The data was recorded at a sampling rate of 48 kHz and a resolution of 32 bits, with a 20 Hz high-pass filter applied to each acquisition channel.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: The recording process was conducted over a period of time with each participant undergoing four steps: speech-clean (15 minutes), speechless-noisy (2 minutes and 24 seconds), speechless-clean (54 seconds), and speech-noisy (54 seconds). The dataset includes recordings from 188 participants, with the total duration of the 6-channel recordings being over 45 hours per sensor.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: The dataset underwent post-processing to enhance data quality and facilitate interpretability. This included applying a series of three automatic filters to remove utterances with obvious deficiencies, such as mispronounced sentences, sensor shifting, sensor malfunctions, or microphones being left unequipped. The filters were based on indicators like Phoneme Error Rate (PER), signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), and sound levels during voiced and non-voiced segments. Additionally, timestamps generated by Voice Activity Detection (VAD) were extended by 0.6 seconds on both sides to eliminate unwanted artifacts.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: The preprocessing protocol involved applying a 20 Hz high-pass filter to each acquisition channel to attenuate low-frequency noise and artifacts. The dataset was split into four subsets: speech-clean, speech-noisy, speechless-clean, and speechless-noisy. The speech-clean subset was used for training and evaluation, while the other subsets were used for testing and analysis. The dataset was also split by speaker, with 80% of male and female speakers in the training set, 10% in the development/validation set, and 10% in the test set.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: The dataset includes annotations about the recording conditions and linguistic transcriptions. The text used for participant readings originated from the French Wikipedia subset of Common Voice, which was filtered to produce a simplified dataset with a minimum number of textual and phonemic symbols. The phonetic transcription was generated using the International Phonetic Alphabet (IPA) with 33 phonemes in French. Manual phonetic transcription was performed for unrecognized words.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: The phonetic transcription was generated using the text phonemizer of the CoML lab, and manual phonetic transcription was performed for unrecognized words. The dataset also includes annotations about the recording conditions and linguistic transcriptions.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The dataset includes annotations about the recording conditions and linguistic transcriptions. The phonetic transcription was generated using the International Phonetic Alphabet (IPA) with 33 phonemes in French. Manual phonetic transcription was performed for unrecognized words to ensure accuracy.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: text phonemizer of the CoML lab, Whisper-timestamped model, Levenshtein distance, VAD (Voice Activity Detection), Coherence functions, Power spectral density analysis
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset is publicly available on HuggingFace under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International license. The dataset is versioned and maintained by the Laboratoire de Mécanique des Structures et des Systèmes Couplés (LMSSC) at the Conservatoire National des Arts et Métiers (Cnam), Paris, France.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The dataset is compliant with the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR), and all necessary measures were taken to protect the privacy and rights of participants in this study. This included obtaining informed consent, clearly communicating the purpose of data collection, and ensuring anonymization and encryption of data during storage and analysis.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset aims to advance research in speech capture using non-conventional audio sensors, particularly in noisy environments. It addresses limitations in existing datasets, such as the limited diversity of audio sensors and the lack of noise recordings. The dataset provides a unique combination of simultaneous multi-microphone recordings and French-language data, offering new perspectives for non-conventional speech capture and comparative analyses of different sensor technologies.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset includes recordings from 188 participants, with a deliberate effort to recruit a diverse and gender-balanced group of participants. However, the dataset may still exhibit biases related to the limited number of participants and the specific acoustic conditions imposed by the 3D spatializer.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset has several known limitations, including the limited bandwidth of body-conduction sensors, which restricts their ability to capture high frequencies. The dataset also includes a relatively small number of participants (188) and may not be representative of all possible acoustic scenarios. Additionally, the dataset includes recordings from only one language (French), which may limit its applicability to other languages.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is intended for use in speech-related tasks, including speech recognition, speech enhancement, and speaker verification. It is particularly useful for advancing research in body-conduction audio sensors and robust communication systems in noisy environments. The dataset can be used for training, testing, and validation of machine learning models.
